entries.title: Recursive context-bound evaluator
entries.summary: Shared bounded-cache entry point for the retained interval-cut context evaluator with explicit semantics.
entries.api: evaluator(a, u, k, *, semantics, cache_size=16000) -> cached_bound(word, maxima); compiled semantics: context-bound-zero-children-c-v1
entries.example:
from harness.research.recursive import evaluator
word = ('S', (1, 'lower'), 'S'); maxima = (1,)
bound = evaluator(3, 3, 3, semantics='context-bound-zero-children-v1', cache_size=16000)(word, maxima)
entries.semantics: semantics is required: historical-f2-v1 drops zero-valued children, context-bound-zero-children-v1 includes them in Python, and context-bound-zero-children-c-v1 is the cross-checked compiled implementation of the same arithmetic convention. These are exploratory evaluators, not a certificate of equivalence to Lean or a kernel-compiled proof.

entries.title: Compiled recursive context-bound evaluator
entries.summary: Memoized C implementation of the zero-child interval-cut context recurrence, exposed through the shared evaluator factory.
entries.api: compiled_evaluator(a, u, k, *, cache_size=16000, persistent=False) -> bound(word, maxima); shared API semantics context-bound-zero-children-c-v1
entries.example:
python -m harness.research.context_bound --case 3,4,5 --word 1L,S,S,2U,S,S --maxima 3,1
# many related contexts (e.g. every part of one context): one C memo across calls, ~27x faster
F = compiled_evaluator(5, 5, 6, cache_size=2_000_000, persistent=True)
entries.semantics: Implements the context-bound-zero-children-v1 arithmetic with all declared levels, truncated natural subtraction, zero-valued children retained, and per-call memoization. Exact signed 64-bit results are returned and larger results raise OverflowError. Compilation is cached in an owner-only system temporary directory. An in-flight C call is not preempted by the Python SIGALRM per-case timer, so probe shapes must remain independently bounded. Cross-language tests are finite diagnostic evidence only, not Lean proof credit. persistent=True keeps one C memo across calls for fixed (a, u, k) (word length is part of the key); values are identical to the per-call memo (regression test test_persistent_compiled_memo_returns_the_fresh_memo_values), the memo stops growing at cache_size entries, and close() or garbage collection frees it.

entries.title: Context-side extension length
entries.summary: Computes the longest ordered extension through selected external levels on one side of a position.
entries.api: extension(word, depth, side, p, left) -> int
entries.example:
from harness.research.primitives import extension
length = extension(('S', (1, 'lower'), 'S'), 1, 'lower', 2, True)
entries.semantics: Starts with position p at length zero, scans levels 1..depth whose first marker has the requested side, and extends strictly left or right through their marker positions. It is exploratory rank-primitives-v1 arithmetic and establishes no Lean theorem.

entries.title: Rectangle rank clipping and potential
entries.summary: Clips interval rows to a chosen side and evaluates the retained edge/rectangle potential P.
entries.api: clip(rows, keep, axis) -> clipped_rows; P(rows) -> int
entries.example:
from harness.research.primitives import P, clip
rows = [(1, 2, 1, 3), (2, 3, 2, 4)]
value = P(clip(rows, {0}, 0))
entries.semantics: Rows are four integer endpoints (x-low, x-high, y-low, y-high); axis is 0 or 1. clip retains indexed rows while tightening the selected axis from removed rows. P is the minimum of a sparse edge/unit count and a rectangular rank cap. These abstract intervals are not automatically geometric realizations or Lean proofs.

entries.title: Child context construction
entries.summary: Builds one child row after a cut by retaining selected S positions and inserting a level-one sibling.
entries.api: part(row, keep, side, m) -> child_row
entries.semantics: S positions in keep remain S; every other S becomes a new level-one external marker with the supplied side; prior external levels shift by one and m is prepended to maxima. Global a/u/k/chosen fields are copied unchanged. This constructs exploratory evaluator input, not a geometric witness.

entries.title: Singleton context-cut values
entries.summary: Enumerates both orientations and every admissible coupling at each child, retaining zero-valued parts.
entries.api: singleton_cut_values(evaluate, row) -> list[(sum, position, side, sibling_maximum)]
entries.example:
from harness.research.context_bound import compiled_evaluator
from harness.research.singleton_cuts import singleton_cut_values
row = {'word': ('S', (1, 'lower'), 'S'), 'maxima': (1,), 'a': 4, 'u': 4, 'k': 5, 'chosen': 'lower'}
F = compiled_evaluator(4, 4, 5, persistent=True)
try:
    choices = singleton_cut_values(F, row)
finally:
    F.close()
entries.semantics: Requires integer k>=3 and at least two S positions, a context row accepted by research.context-part, and a callback computing bounds at the row's a/u/k. Exposed callback globals must agree. Enumerates positions in increasing order and lower coupling d=1..k-2, then lower/d and upper/(k-1-d). Every sum is retained, even when one or both parts have value zero; errors including evaluator overflow propagate. The caller owns cache, resource guards and outputs. With the compiled evaluator results are diagnostic context-bound-zero-children-c-v1 arithmetic, not kernel proofs of singleton attainment. Retained source and checked-in values: R13 probes and harness/research/examples/singleton-cuts-v1.json.

entries.title: Ordered rectangle cover bound
entries.summary: Computes the minimum additive rectangular cover bound over consecutive blocks.
entries.api: ordered_cover(record) -> int
entries.semantics: Each rectangle is (label, x-low, x-high, y-low, y-high). Dynamic programming partitions the ordered list into consecutive blocks and sums (|X|-1)(|Y|-1)+1 for each block. The value is an exploratory combinatorial bound, not proof credit.

entries.title: Indexed-maximum candidate bounds
entries.summary: Returns every retained candidate bound triggered by a context row's indexed sibling maxima.
entries.api: maximum_bounds(row) -> list[{bound, reason, level}]
entries.semantics: Applies the retained k-2, k-3, k-4 and younger-marker formulas level by level, choosing the opposite global cap/cup parameter from the marker side. Returned inequalities are exploratory candidates and must be proved separately in Lean.

entries.title: Sole opposite-level normalization
entries.summary: Normalizes a context whose only level opposite the chosen side is level one.
entries.api: sole_opposite_normalize(row) -> normalized_row
entries.semantics: Requires level one to be opposite chosen and every later level not opposite. It removes the first maximum, rotates level-one markers to the former maximum depth, decrements other marker levels, and tightens the corresponding a/u parameter to k-n. Preconditions are asserted; the transform is exploratory, not a proved equivalence.

entries.title: Context signature constraint evaluator
entries.summary: Converts a tagged sweep word and sibling maxima into per-run cup and cap limits.
entries.api: limits_from_signature(word, maxima, a, u, k, *, lean=False) -> (run_count, cup_limits, cap_limits)
entries.example:
sys.path.insert(0, 'scripts')
from decomposable_depth2_tables import limits_from_signature
p, cups, caps = limits_from_signature(word, maxima, a, u, k, lean=True)
entries.semantics: The matrices bound chains spanning each ordered pair of child runs. lean=True includes unused levels, uses unbounded integers, and truncates subtraction at zero. This legacy exploratory calculation is not a kernel-compiled theorem or proof of equivalence to Lean.

entries.title: Abstract context and split enumeration
entries.summary: Generates bounded tagged contexts and constructs child signatures for arbitrary vertex splits.
entries.api: contexts(s_max, e_max, levels, k, *, include_unused_levels=False); child(word, maxima, keep, side_of_child, sibling_max)
entries.example:
sys.path.insert(0, 'scripts')
from decomposable_additivity_test import contexts, child
for word, maxima in contexts(4, 2, 2, 5): ...
entries.semantics: contexts yields finite abstract signatures with consecutive occupied levels by default. child retains selected S positions, turns the complement into a new level-one sibling, and shifts existing external levels. Enumeration output has no kernel proof credit.

entries.title: Exact compiled-class context evaluator
entries.summary: Evaluates the largest compiled decomposable coloring satisfying one abstract context signature.
entries.api: load_class(class_dir, max_n) -> tables; exact(tables, a, u, k, word, maxima, max_n) -> int
entries.example:
sys.path.insert(0, 'scripts')
from decomposable_context_exact import load_class, exact
tables = load_class(class_dir, max_n); value = exact(tables, a, u, k, word, maxima, max_n)
entries.semantics: Searches generated class data from max_n downward and returns the first stored size meeting every per-run cup/cap limit and the strong-set limit; returns zero when no stored size qualifies. Compiled-class here means the enumerator's data format, not a Lean kernel-compiled proof.

entries.title: Exact decomposable coloring enumeration
entries.summary: Enumerates the abstract decomposable triple-coloring class and computes reusable chain profiles.
entries.api: enumerate_class(max_n, progress=True) -> (classes, triple_indices); coloring_dict(mask, n, index); chain_profiles(coloring, n, left)
entries.example:
sys.path.insert(0, 'scripts')
from enumerate_decomposable_colorings import enumerate_class
classes, triple_indices = enumerate_class(7, progress=False)
entries.semantics: Builds labeled colorings recursively over every ordered nonempty bipartition, fixes crossing triples by the deep-below rule, and deduplicates bitmasks at each size. These Python enumeration results remain exploratory until represented and checked in Lean.

entries.title: Captured proof checking and finite proving
entries.summary: Use the harness to freeze a proof span, check a candidate, or try the registered finite tactic portfolio.
entries.api: es proof capture NODE [--start BYTE --end BYTE]; es proof check FIXTURE --body FILE; es proof prove FIXTURE [--tactics TACTIC]
entries.example:
es proof capture ErdosSzekeres.someNode
es proof check FIXTURE_ID --body runs/candidate.lean
entries.semantics: Capture freezes source and dependency identities. Checks run in an isolated pinned Lean environment and accept only a complete parent with the expected type and allowed axioms; prove uses a finite registered tactic portfolio.

entries.title: Checked node finalization for review
entries.summary: Validate and insert a proof body, run targeted and full checks, audit it, and prepare one node for review.
entries.api: es node finish NODE --body FILE [--fixture FIXTURE] [--window WINDOW] [--extract-memory SIZE]
entries.example: es node finish ErdosSzekeres.someNode --body runs/candidate.lean --fixture FIXTURE_ID --window WINDOW_ID
entries.semantics: Runs the review-only finalization policy: preflight source checks, isolated candidate validation, insertion into the original node, targeted check, full extraction, and audit. Completion prepares review state; inspect the durable operation result before claiming theorem closure.

entries.title: Versioned bounded probe and witness replay
entries.summary: Run a registered finite research probe with source pinning, budgets, durable results, and witness replay.
entries.api: es probe run --spec SPEC.json [--window WINDOW]; es probe replay RESULT_ARTIFACT
entries.example:
es probe run --spec runs/probe-spec.json --window WINDOW_ID
es probe replay RESULT_ARTIFACT_ID
entries.semantics: Admission pins registered plugin sources and an explicit semantic version. Execution enforces finite case/time budgets; negative results receive no proof credit, and saved witnesses replay under the same source version.

entries.title: Bounded two-marker recursive-cut probe
entries.summary: Run or replay the registered deterministic two-lower-marker cut family through the shared recursive evaluator.
entries.api: es probe run --spec harness/research/examples/recursive-cut-small.json [--window WINDOW]; es probe replay RESULT_ARTIFACT
entries.example:
es probe run --spec harness/research/examples/recursive-cut-small.json --window WINDOW_ID
es probe replay RESULT_ARTIFACT_ID
entries.semantics: Uses plugin recursive_cut, domain two-lower-marker-cut-family-v1, generator extreme-next-deterministic-v1, split rule nonempty-proper-child-subsets-with-geometry-v1, and candidate matched-coupling-budgets-v1. Both registered recursion semantics are retained evaluators only: every result sets Lean equivalence, Lean refutation, and finite-negative proof credit to false.

entries.title: Source-identified node context bundle
entries.summary: Retrieve compact theorem state, dependency signatures, recent outcomes, and an explicit freshness verdict.
entries.api: es context NODE [--previous BUNDLE_ARTIFACT]
entries.example:
es context ErdosSzekeres.someNode
es context ErdosSzekeres.someNode --previous PRIOR_BUNDLE_ID
entries.semantics: The bundle records the node, current source hash, selected compiled-index dependency signatures, recent events and operations. A previous bundle produces a compact delta; frontier_fresh remains explicit.

entries.title: Research windows, usage accounting, and handoff
entries.summary: Record research windows, import exact local usage, compare matched work, and generate factual handoffs.
entries.api: es run begin LABEL; es usage sync --window WINDOW; es run end WINDOW [--accepted N]; es run handoff --window WINDOW
entries.example:
window=$(es run begin recursive-bound-audit)
es usage sync --window "$window"
es run end "$window" --accepted 1
entries.semantics: Usage is imported from recorded local response events without conversation text. Budgets are observational, comparisons require matched windows, and handoffs report durable operation state plus measured usage coverage.

entries.title: Bounded durable Sol research run
entries.summary: Run one Sol/xhigh native goal with fixed deadlines, guarded jobs, durable recovery and usage accounting.
entries.api: es run agent --out runs/RUN --prompt /absolute/prompt.md [--model gpt-5.6-sol --effort xhigh --hours 12]; es run agent-status runs/RUN; es run agent --out runs/RUN --resume
entries.example:
es run agent --out runs/sol-trial --prompt /absolute/path/research-prompt.md --model gpt-5.6-sol --effort xhigh --hours 12
es run agent-status runs/sol-trial
entries.semantics: The 2 GiB host owns a separate Codex native-goal session. A frozen research deadline permits one bounded finalization turn afterward. The worker registers a run observer. Manual resume is explicit; a configured bounded automatic capacity-only retry requires fresh serverOverloaded evidence and rechecks the current goal before recovery. Neither route extends deadlines; uncertain receipts are not automatically replayed. Job completion alone confers no theorem credit or current-client notification guarantee.

entries.title: Register and elaborate a Lean statement
entries.summary: Create a statement through the harness with a narrow import and enough memory for nested elaboration.
entries.api: es node add --name NAME --ws B --kind formalization --type SIGNATURE --description TEXT --consumer NODE --import MODULE [--targeted]
entries.example:
es node add --help
# Without the user bus, queue this command through es job run.
# The elaboration cap is sized to the import closure (4-5G for thin blueprint nodes);
# the enclosing job must still fit a retry at build.memory_max (20G). Full extraction needs 28G.
entries.semantics: Node registration writes a sorry only in ESBlueprint and elaborates the statement before locking it. Search and claim first. Elaboration and the targeted extract run under caps sized to the module's import closure (elaboration_memory_max: 3G + 4 x closure olean GiB, floor 4G; targeted extract: 3G + 2 x GiB, floor 4G, ceiling extract.targeted_memory_max); a dependency without an olean, or one `lake build --no-build` reports stale, gets the full build.memory_max, and an OOM kill under the sized cap is retried once at the full cap. An enclosing job smaller than the full cap refuses that retry. It leaves the full frontier stale, so refresh before selecting further research. Use the smallest import closure that supplies the statement.

entries.title: Commit one node's files on its node branch
entries.summary: Stage exactly one node's module, root import, lock/index records and falsifier, check whitespace, and commit; from a sandbox the commit is queued for es worker.
entries.api: es node commit NODE [--message TEXT | --message-file FILE] [--include runs/...]
entries.example:
es node commit ctx_bound_reverse --message-file runs/r3/COMMIT.txt
# In a Codex sandbox (read-only .git-data) this prints a queued job id:
es job wait <id> --timeout 55
entries.semantics: Refuses unless HEAD is a node/ branch other than the default, and unless the index is empty beforehand. Stages only the node's files that changed (module, blueprint root, statements.lock, nodes.json, status.md, index.json, falsifier and its harness/falsify record) plus --include artifacts under runs/ or data/; runs git diff --cached --check and unstages on problems. When the git metadata is not writable it queues `es node commit --direct` as a 1G job of kind commit (lock git:<root>, not a build slot) for es worker. It never merges or pushes.

entries.title: Guarded commands and terminal receipts
entries.summary: Run existing scripts with shared memory admission, job identity, declared outputs, bounded waits, progress-review checkpoints and cancellation.
entries.api: es job run --why PURPOSE --out runs/OUTPUT --mem SIZE [--review MIN] -- COMMAND; es job wait JOB --timeout 55; es job review JOB --note TEXT [--next MIN]; es job status JOB
entries.example:
es job run --why 'record interpreter version' --out runs/python-version.txt --mem 256M -- bash -c 'python3 --version > runs/python-version.txt'
es job wait JOB_ID --timeout 55
entries.semantics: Submission is not completion. Inspect the terminal receipt including outputs_missing; --out declares an artifact but does not redirect stdout. Never kill a research computation at a self-chosen time: time a small instance first, make the job print progress (done/total, rate) to its log or an --out file, and set --review from the estimate. When es job wait returns review_due, read the progress, estimate the time left, and record the decision with es job review (leave it; make it cheaper; or answer another way, keeping the question); a checkpoint never stops the job, and --budget kills only for a deadline the user set. A stopped or narrowed run is not a result: log its coverage and the follow-up. Prefer direct argv; a shell pipeline must enable pipefail so output capture cannot hide command failure. Nested Lean commands need an enclosing reservation large enough for their configured build and extraction caps. For direct Git commands use -c gc.auto=0 -c maintenance.auto=false to keep automatic background maintenance from retaining the scope; unknown execution must be reconciled, never blindly retried.

entries.title: Verified immutable certificate artifact sharing
entries.summary: Deduplicate identical compiled certificate outputs across compatible checkouts sharing one harness database, using Lake's native immutable cache.
entries.api: es storage share --other CHECKOUT [--apply] [--cache PATH] [--receipt runs/FILE.jsonl] [--facet FACET]
entries.example:
es job run --why "verify immutable certificate duplicates" --out runs/storage-share/audit.jsonl --mem 4G --budget 90 -- tools/es/bin/es storage share --other runs/worktrees/sol-12h-20260916 --receipt runs/storage-share/audit.jsonl
# Add --apply to the inner command to adopt verified blobs.
entries.semantics: Requires a guarded job, compatible project/toolchain/filesystem, and generated certificate modules in both checkouts. The default is verification only. Full SHA-256 checks precede atomic hard-link adoption through the pinned Lake cache; sources and mutable setup/trace/hash sidecars are excluded. Both worktrees and the shared cache are reserved. Receipts separate logical duplicate bytes, eligible freed blocks and observed free-space change. Native input mappings are created only by ordinary guarded Lake builds, never synthesized from filenames. Rebuild detachment was tested on pinned Lean 4.29.1; unsupported toolchains are refused.

entries.title: Audited Lake setup metadata cleanup
entries.summary: Inventory or prune Lake 4.29.1 setup spill files with exact-path manifests, inode revalidation and storage exclusion.
entries.api: es storage prune-setup [--apply] [--out runs/DIRECTORY]
entries.example:
es storage prune-setup --out runs/setup-audit
# Inspect runs/setup-audit/manifest.json, then:
es storage prune-setup --apply --out runs/setup-prune
entries.semantics: Dry-run is the default. The pinned Lake 4.29.1 contract scans only a real .lake/build/ir directory without symlink traversal, writes the manifest durably, revalidates every regular-file identity before unlinking, and reports logical removed bytes separately from allocated blocks actually made unreachable by hard-link counts. Automatic post-build cleanup considers only modules in successful acknowledged Lake Built records while its worktree reservation remains held. Plugin and dynlib paths inside a setup snapshot are references and are never removed. A killed standalone maintenance process may leave a conservative lease for explicit reconciliation; no bulk cleanup is implied by enabling the command.

entries.title: Run observation without model polling
entries.summary: Observe durable research jobs in the worker and escalate only a terminal run or persistent infrastructure blocker.
entries.api: es run watch OUT; es run progress OUT [--follow 55]; es run observe; es run unwatch OUT
entries.example:
es run progress runs/sol-trial
es run progress runs/sol-trial --follow 55
es run observe
es delivery status
entries.semantics: Native run submission registers automatically. Idle observations and individual compiler failures make no model requests. If a host runner disappears after its recorded cgroup has definitely stopped, the observer reconciles the stale job row with a compare-and-set on the recorded runner identity and emits the terminal event once; a changed or live runner remains reserved. A configured bounded retry handles only a fresh provider capacity failure within the frozen deadline; it never resets pause, quota, cancellation or uncertain effects. Unwatch stops observation without cancelling compute or messages already queued. Unattended reporting requires a separately verified callback plus an available worker.

entries.title: Final research accounting and code inventory
entries.summary: Collect deduplicated late usage, direct jobs, validation evidence and code review inventory in one immutable bundle.
entries.api: es run review OUT [--artifact-root RUN_DIR]; build_review(cfg, out, compact_limit=4096, artifact_root=None)
entries.example: es run review runs/sol-trial/host --artifact-root runs/sol-trial
entries.semantics: Summary is bounded to 4096 bytes; full evidence is immutable. Usage includes finalization after the research window closes and reports source limits. Explicit artifact roots must contain the host directory under configured output roots; otherwise the inventory states its host-only coverage. Source hashes and sanitized inline commands support review; scripts are not executed. Operational success never grants theorem credit. Final mathematical review is always required, with code review flagged separately.

entries.title: Verified exact-thread completion callbacks
entries.summary: Verify the actual receiving Codex thread before submitting compact run-level events through its queue.
entries.api: es delivery status; es delivery verify --thread UUID; es delivery confirm --challenge TOKEN; es delivery abandon-verification --thread UUID
entries.example:
es delivery status
es delivery verify --thread "$CODEX_THREAD_ID"
# Confirm only the challenge actually received through this thread.
entries.semantics: Queue acceptance alone does not verify receipt. Confirmation requires the unchanged receiving CODEX_THREAD_ID and coordinator identity. Packets are at most 2048 bytes plus the event marker; full evidence stays in immutable artifacts. Events have a separate outbox from operation delivery. Uncertain submissions are never automatically retried; abandoning a verification invalidates its nonce but cannot cancel an already queued message. Transport configuration does not override the client model, permissions or quota.

entries.title: Signotope point-set cubes and Knuth cube-tree estimates
entries.summary: Legal rank-3 signotope patterns on point sets as SAT cubes (ETV triple numbering), reversal symmetry, and a solver-agnostic Knuth random-walk tree-size estimator for choosing a cube order and depth.
entries.api: patterns_on(points) -> [pattern]; extensions(pattern, points, new) -> [new triples]; place(pattern, points); lits_of(pattern, N) -> [int]; triple_var(t, N) -> int; reverse(pattern, N); knuth_walk(order, roots, start_depth, survives, is_leaf, rng, max_depth=None) -> [step]; knuth_estimates(walks) -> dict
entries.example:
from harness.research import signotope_cubes as sc
cubes = [sc.lits_of(p, 27) for p in sc.patterns_on([13, 12, 14, 11, 15, 10])]  # 908 level-6 cubes, center-outward
# survives = lambda p: <python-sat conf_budget(1) solve is not False>; is_leaf = lambda p, d: <20k-conflict attempt refutes>
walk = sc.knuth_walk(order, roots, 6, survives, is_leaf, random.Random(0))
entries.semantics: Patterns map sorted triples to bool; legality is only the one-change (rank-3 signotope) law on every 4-subset, so pattern counts on 1..7 points are 1,1,2,8,62,908,24698 (OEIS A006245, regression-tested). Cup/cap/convex-gon constraints are NOT applied: the caller filters with its CNF (e.g. a propagation test). triple_var matches scripts/generate_etv_tseitin_sat.py (1 + index in combinations(range(N),3), tested against the generator). reverse maps legal patterns to legal patterns and preserves cups/caps; whether it is a symmetry of a given CNF must be checked per encoding (verified for the ETV CNF in runs/etv-cc-20260930/verify_reversal.py). knuth_walk is Knuth's unbiased estimator: 10**log10_prod at the last step estimates the leaf count; single walks are heavy-tailed, so report medians with means. python-sat pitfalls: conf_budget(0) means no limit; CaDiCaL has no propagate(); keep each incremental solver on one cube point set (mixing sets was ~10x slower). Diagnostic tooling only; no proof output.

entries.title: Cup/cap chains and strong sets of a triple colouring
entries.summary: Longest chains, chain enumeration, per-edge and endpoint-pair chain tables with witnesses, maximum-chain cores (L*, R*), and the largest strong set via the cup+cap formula with a 4-point brute-force reference.
entries.api: longest_chain(cup, points, want) -> int; chains(cup, t, want, points) -> [tuple]; edge_chain_tables(cup, n, want) -> (end, start); longest_lr(cup, points, want) -> {(l, r): (length, chain)}; chain_core(cup, points, want) -> (L*, R*, max chains); strong_number(cup, points) -> int; strong_number_bruteforce(cup, points) -> int; is_strong(cup, points) -> bool; is_one_change(cup, points) -> bool
entries.example:
from harness.research.chains import longest_chain, strong_number
cup = {(0, 1, 2): True}  # sorted triple -> True = cup
longest_chain(cup, range(3), True), longest_chain(cup, range(3), False), strong_number(cup, range(3))  # (3, 2, 3)
# python3 harness/research/examples/strong_gons_demo.py
entries.semantics: Points are integers in sweep order; cup maps each sorted triple to True (cup, left turn, set bit in decomposable.coloring-enumeration masks) or False (cap). A chain's consecutive triples all have its colour; sets of <= 2 points are both cups and caps (lengths 0, 1, 2), so a limit of 1 admits one point. Strong set = Lean IsStrongPolygonSet (4-point definition); sets of <= 3 points are strong. strong_number uses max(min(n,3), cup_lr + cap_lr - 2 over endpoint pairs), which equals the 4-point definition on one-change colourings (all 908 six-point signotopes and random decomposable sets regression-tested) and is NOT valid on arbitrary colourings; strong_number_bruteforce and is_strong hold for any colouring (exponential, small sets). chain_core gives L* = max first point and R* = min last point over the longest chains (interior core when L* < R*). Diagnostic computation only; no Lean proof.

entries.title: Lazy strong-set (gon) witness and CEGAR two-colouring
entries.summary: Finds one strong set of an exact size without enumerating gons, and two-colours points so that neither class contains a strong size-set by adding gon clauses lazily to a SAT solver.
entries.api: find_gon(cup, points, size) -> sorted tuple | None; cegar_two_colouring(cup, points, hard, size) -> (blue, red) | None
entries.example:
from harness.research.chains import find_gon, cegar_two_colouring
gon = find_gon(s.cup, range(s.n), k - 1)  # None: no strong (k-1)-set in s
res = cegar_two_colouring(s.cup, list(range(s.n)), hard_clauses, k - 1)  # SAT var p+1 true = blue
entries.semantics: find_gon pairs a longest cup and a longest cap with the same endpoints and trims interior points to the exact size; it is complete (None means no strong size-set) only on one-change colourings, regression-tested against strong_number_bruteforce on all 908 six-point signotopes, and raises ValueError if a cup and cap share an interior point. Memory O(|S|^2) per start point; about 31 MB per k=8 sample in runs/claude-hypergraph-20261003, versus one clause pair per gon. cegar_two_colouring needs python-sat (Cadical195): variable p+1 is point p (non-negative integers; true = blue); hard is the caller's clause list; while a colour class holds a size-gon it adds the clauses forbidding that gon to be monochromatic and re-solves; returns (blue, red) with both classes strong-size-free, or None when none exists (agreement with brute force over all 2^n colourings is regression-tested). Diagnostic only; no proof output.

entries.title: Decomposable sets as binary label trees
entries.summary: Builds decomposable colourings from prefix-free root-path labels, composes, splits and samples them, decides exact decomposability of any colouring, converts enumerator bitmasks, and evaluates decomposableThreshold.
entries.api: DecomposableSet(labels) -> .n .cup .alpha .beta .strong .end .st, .longest(sub, want), .chains(t, want, sub), .cap_core(), .cup_core(), .root_split(); coloring_from_labels(labels); check_labels(labels); normalize_labels(labels); compose(A, B, lowerpos); root_split(labels); random_labels(n, rng); random_nested_labels(n, rng, pnest=0.6); all_splits(cup, pts); Decomposability(cup).dec(pts) / .splits(pts); coloring_from_mask(mask, n); mask_from_coloring(cup, n); decomposable_masks(max_n); threshold(a, u, k)
entries.example:
from harness.research.decomposable_sets import DecomposableSet, random_nested_labels
s = DecomposableSet(random_nested_labels(14, random.Random(2026)))
s.alpha, s.beta, s.strong  # cup, cap and strong numbers: 5, 7, 8
# python3 harness/research/examples/band_partitions_demo.py
entries.semantics: Decomposable = IsDecomposableOn (singleton, or nonempty lower A and upper B, interleaved arbitrarily, a triple meeting both is a cup iff its middle point is in A). Point p carries its root path ('0' lower, '1' upper); labels must be distinct and prefix-free (checked; SAT-decoded 0/1 tuples are normalised). Triple p<q<r is a cup iff the middle label has '0' where the three first differ. Label trees generate exactly the enumerated class on n <= 6, and Decomposability accepts exactly 718 of the 908 six-point signotopes (both regression-tested); it is exponential in |pts|. DecomposableSet keeps the attribute names of runs/claude-bandrule-20261003/bl.py S; chain conventions as research.cup-cap-chains (sets of <= 2 points are both cups and caps). decomposable_masks wraps decomposable.coloring-enumeration (class counts 2, 8, 62, 718, 10596 for n = 3..7 tested; 186888, 3816380 for n = 8, 9 from the audit). threshold mirrors Lean decomposableThreshold with truncated subtraction and equals the exact maximum (cap <= a-1, cup <= u-1, strong <= k-1) in all 139 cases decided by n <= 7 enumeration. Diagnostic only; no Lean proof.

entries.title: BDL band partitions: exact search, verifier, SAT cross-check
entries.summary: Enumerates or finds band partitions (band j: cup <= j+1, cap <= k-1-j) over the BDL range with optional per-point band restrictions, verifies them independently, and re-decides by SAT.
entries.api: bdl_range(alpha, beta, k) -> [j]; band_limits(j, k) -> (j+1, k-1-j); partitions(cup, points, k, bands, *, allowed=None, limit=None, first=False) -> [tuple]; find_partition(cup, points, k, bands, *, allowed=None) -> tuple | None; check_partition(cup, points, k, b, bands=None) -> bool; allowed_from_forbid(points, bands, forbid) -> {p: bands}; partition_sat(cup, points, k, bands, *, allowed=None) -> tuple | None
entries.example:
from harness.research.band_partitions import bdl_range, find_partition, check_partition
bands = bdl_range(s.alpha, s.beta, k)  # k-1-cap .. cup-1
b = find_partition(s.cup, range(s.n), k, bands)  # b[p] = band of point p, or None
assert b is None or check_partition(s.cup, range(s.n), k, b, bands)
entries.semantics: A band partition puts every point in a band j whose members have cup <= j+1 and cap <= k-1-j; with the chain convention that sets of <= 2 points are both cups and caps, only bands 0..k-2 can be used and bands 0 and k-2 hold at most one point. bdl_range(alpha, beta, k) = k-1-beta .. alpha-1; BDL asserts a partition in that range for decomposable X with strong(X) <= k-1 and cup+cap >= k (cup+cap = k is the one-band case). Results are tuples aligned with sorted(points) (b[p] for range(n)); bands are tried in the given order; allowed[p] restricts point p (allowed_from_forbid builds it from forbidden points per band, e.g. the P invariant's bottom band j0 = k-1-cap inside x <= L*). partitions is complete backtracking with incremental chain tables; check_partition recomputes every band from scratch; partition_sat (python-sat Cadical195, lazy import) is a second exact method that agrees with backtracking (regression-tested). Fixture examples/band-partitions-v1.json freezes the exhaustive audit counts (pairs, multi-band, P, PF, P', cores) for n <= 7, reproduced exactly; BDL holds on all decomposable colourings with n <= 9 per runs/claude-audit-bdl-20261003. Diagnostic computation, not a Lean proof of BDL.
